Because spirit is the invisible half of nature, we learn much about spirit by observing nature closely and participating in it intimately. We observe the cycle of the seasons, for instance, and see how the changes of increase and decrease are inevitable—yet the precise timing of their arrival...

title: A New I Ching for the New Dynasty
excerpt: The Spirit of the Age has reversed course again and we have entered a new Dynasty. Unlike the dynasties of old that ruled one nation or one people, this time it is an egalitarian Dynasty, a global shift of awareness, setting free the potential of all nations and all people for the next 5,000 years. The old Dynasty of nationalism, aggression and self-interest is overturned now by time. In its place, like billions of seeds fallen on the fertile plain of history...

title: Returning to the Ancestral Future
excerpt: The future draws us forward with our own creations. While governments, corporations and the media collude to create an official future of preemptive authoritarianism, individual powerlessness and collective alienation, they unwittingly trigger the pandemic backlash of an unofficial future rooted in the sacred human. A significant thrust of this global backlash springs from the combining and reinterpreting of cultural creations that have long carried people’s hearts and minds toward a future of universal peace and prospering...

Just such a juncture in history has arisen, however, to test this generation’s will to set aside the failed visions of the past...

title: The Art of Long-term Relationships
excerpt: Relationships are living organisms—they breathe, grow, and change constantly. Maintaining long-term connections requires a deep awareness of oneself and the other, a willingness to cultivate patience, generosity, and understanding, and a readiness to adapt without losing the integrity of the bond. This requires conscious effort and ethical engagement.

We follow in the hope it's leading us to a flock we can photograph before the afternoon rain sets in. The first warning drops splash dust on the washboard road as a flock of ibis flap madly against the north wind.

title: Echoes of Presence
excerpt: Remember when we were young and played with bugs, sensing them with their feelers? I was born in a cemetery and lived among the hills and stones, sensing presence everywhere. This first-hand experience of pure awareness forms the foundation of nature mysticism, spiritual transformation, and the mind within the mind.

title: The Ithaca Oracle
excerpt: The emerging world culture calls to all; Take Your Stand In The Inevitable! In Ithaca, New York, a group Oracle explored harmony between people, nature, and spirit. Through coin tosses and Hexagrams 16 and 17, participants received guidance on maintaining inner flexibility, trust, and alignment with universal principles.

title: Five Keys to Inspired Action in the Global Spring
excerpt: The movement from me to we is well underway. A new lifeway is spreading, inspiring social and environmental ethics. Generations awaken, old hatreds pass, and a shared vision of possibility emerges. By recapturing principles, fostering self-sacrifice, radiating spirit and intent, and unifying inspiration, people contribute joyfully to the collective good.

title: The Tao of Enlightenment
excerpt: The concept of the Tao has profoundly impacted world culture, giving rise to Taoist religion, cosmology, art, and Zen practices. Through inward training, meditation, and attunement to the Way, practitioners cultivate awareness beyond words, experiencing the mind within the mind and achieving a natural state of enlightenment and harmony.

title: The Tao of Axolotl
excerpt: At the end of the last Age, the gods gathered at Teotihuacan to create this Age. Xolotl, the god of twins, avoided sacrifice, transforming into maguey, corn, and finally the axolotl. The creature symbolizes the Ancient Child, integrating creativity and independence, retaining curiosity while remaining capable of producing the next generation.

title: I Ching Mathematics
excerpt: I Ching Mathematics: The Science of Change extends divinatory interpretations through mathematical permutations of hexagrams and line changes. Culminating 45 years of study, it enriches the diviner's repertoire and applies to both the Toltec I Ching and standard King Wen version, offering a rational-mystical framework for understanding the Oracle’s guidance.

title: The World Savings Initiative
excerpt: A global mechanism is proposed to exert collective self-governance, giving everyone a vote regardless of contribution. By pooling resources through a trust, people can address systemic problems ignored by the few. Local action and ethical coordination amplify our collective power, demonstrating human ingenuity, goodwill, and the possibility of meaningful global change.

title: Lessons From The Toltec I Ching
excerpt: I am part of a Living Whole that wants the best for me and all others at the same time. Inspired action flows spontaneously from an inspired mind. By clearing selfish and self-defeating thoughts, we open to ethical lessons, attuning to Spirit and the timeless wisdom of the ancients.

title: The Tao Of Green, Part Two
excerpt: The inevitable fully green society depends on transforming human nature rather than institutions. Taoism teaches harmony with the Way, recognizing the sacred in all matter and spirit. By embodying contentment, balancing extremes, and respecting the sacredness of life, individuals align with the One and act with enlightened self-interest.

title: The Tao Of Green
excerpt: The inevitable transition to a fully-green society requires a transformation of human nature. By embracing the ethics of Taoism—working for the benefit of all, sharing without accumulating, and harmonizing with nature—we cultivate self-discipline, trust, and a collective vision, fostering a sustainable and equitable global society.

title: Inspired Action [2]
excerpt: Inspired Action arises spontaneously from each moment, responding to circumstances with clarity and collaboration. Rooted in Flower-and-Song philosophy, it demands presence, discernment, and courage. By perceiving matter and spirit as unified, a spirit warrior ennobles life, acts ethically, and participates in creation, transforming the ordinary into the extraordinary.

title: Celebrating Passage
excerpt: Hexagram 19 celebrates life in all stages. Four warriors dance in joy, symbolizing child, youth, adult, and elder. Their ritual honors the sacredness of existence, immersing us in the oneness of creation. Each moment becomes a celebration, embodying presence, gratitude, and the spirit warrior's wholehearted engagement with life.

title: The World Psyche
excerpt: The World Psyche explores the unity of all souls, emphasizing sensitivity to the unseen forces of nature and humanity. Hexagram 2, Sensing Creation, illustrates the courage and awareness required to engage fully with life, nurturing others and participating in the ongoing evolution of the collective spirit.
